intro: The Black-Iron Gate reopens. The debt-ledger is exposed — every transaction, every bargain, every debt ever recorded. The Hollow has begun erasing entries. In the Infernal Gate, erased debts do not disappear. They become unowned.
The erased debts are becoming unowned obligations — bindings with no creditor and no debtor. They float through the Gate, attaching to anyone who touches them.
The unowned obligations are multiplying. Each one that attaches to a traveler becomes their debt — unearned, unasked, but binding. The trial road is covered in floating debts.
The ledger's core. The first transaction — the original debt that created the Infernal Gate. The Hollow has erased it. Without the original debt, the entire ledger system is destabilizing.
enemy: Unowned obligations — floating debts with no creditor. They attach on contact. Once attached, they are binding.
The obligations are combining into compound debts. The compound debt is heavier and harder to avoid.
Hollow debt-collectors. They do not collect — they assign. They attach unowned obligations to the deity deliberately.

The erased original debt's guardian — a Hollow wearing the first debtor's chains. It speaks the erased transaction's terms — but the terms are corrupted. The original debt was voluntary. The corrupted terms are mandatory.
mid: The unowned obligations attach on contact. Do not touch them — fight around them. Or take ownership to control them — but ownership means accepting the debt.
The compound debts are heavier. Do not avoid them — assign them. Restore the creditor — even if the creditor is you. A debt with an owner is controllable.
The debt-collectors assign obligations. Do not resist — re-assign. Transfer the unowned to the Hollow. The Hollow created them. Let the Hollow own them.
The guardian speaks corrupted terms. Do not argue — restore the original. The original debt was voluntary. The corruption makes it mandatory. Restore consent.
victory: The first ledger section is stabilized. The erased debts are re-owned — but the ledger is vast. The Hollow has learned which debts you take and which you assign.
The unowned obligations are controlled — but more are being erased. The ledger is deteriorating faster than it can be restored.
The debt-collectors are reassigned — but their assignment technique is recorded. The deeper chambers will have better assigners.
The original debt is partially restored — but the terms are still corrupted. The voluntary nature is remembered, but the corruption has made it feel mandatory.
defeat: The unowned obligations attached to you. You tried to avoid them. Return when taking ownership is more powerful than avoidance.
The compound debts were too heavy. You tried to carry them. Return when assigning is more powerful than carrying.
The debt-collectors assigned too many obligations. You resisted instead of re-assigning. Return when transfer is more powerful than resistance.
The guardian's corrupted terms held. You argued with the corruption. Return when restoring consent is more powerful than arguing with coercion.
codex: The Black-Iron Gate tests whether the deity can navigate a system of debts where creditors have been erased. Unowned debts are dangerous because they attach to anyone. The defense is ownership.
The unowned obligations are the Hollow's most insidious Infernal weapon: debts with no creditor and no debtor. The defense is assignment — transfer the unowned to the Hollow.

The debt-collectors assign obligations. The defense is re-assignment. The Infernal Gate is a system of transfers. The Hollow exploits by erasing creditors. The deity restores by becoming the creditor.
The original debt was voluntary. The Hollow corrupted it to mandatory. The difference is consent. Without consent, the transaction is not a debt. It is a theft.

intro: The Debt-Market. The Infernal Gate's trading floor has been breached. The Hollow is not stealing debts — it is giving them away. Free debts. Unowned. Unbinding.
The free debts are destabilizing the market. Every debt given away becomes unowned — and unowned debts attach to travelers. The market is flooding with free obligations.
The flooding has reached the trial road. Free debts cover every surface. Each one is a temptation — useful, if owned. But owning a free debt means accepting obligation without consent.
The market's core. The original ledger — the first record of the first transaction. The Hollow is erasing it line by line. Each erased line releases a free debt.
enemy: Free-debt wraiths — unowned obligations given away by the Hollow. They are lighter than erased debts — but 'freely' by the Hollow means 'without consent from either party.'
The free debts are flooding the market. Each one is a temptation. The Hollow's gifts are never free. The freedom is the trap.
Hollow debt-givers offering free debts to the deity. Each one looks useful, each one is binding. The acceptance is the trap — by accepting, the deity consents to the Hollow's system.
The original ledger's guardian — a Hollow erasing the ledger line by line, speaking the erased transactions as it erases them.
mid: The free-debt wraiths are lighter. Do not accept them — even the useful ones. The Hollow's gifts are binding. The binding is in the acceptance, not the debt.
The flooding market is a temptation. Do not own the free debts. Owning a free debt means accepting the Hollow's system.
The debt-givers offer useful obligations. Do not accept — and do not refuse. Refusing acknowledges the system. Ignore the offer. Ignored debts become unowned.
The guardian erases consensual debts as free. Do not stop the erasing — restore the consent. Each erased line was a consensual transaction. Restore consent and the debt re-owns itself.
victory: The market's first section is stabilized. The free debts are re-owned — but the flooding continues. The deeper chambers will have more free debts.
The free-debt wraiths are controlled — but the temptation remains. The deeper chambers will offer more useful free debts.
The debt-givers are ignored — but their offers echo. The deeper chambers will have louder offers.
The original ledger is partially restored. The consensual transactions are re-owned — but the erasing continues.
defeat: The free-debt wraiths were too light. You accepted them. Return when the lightness of the Hollow's gifts is the warning.
The flooding market tempted you with useful debts. You owned them. Return when useful and binding is more dangerous than useless and free.
The debt-givers' offers were too good. You accepted or refused. Return when ignoring is more powerful than either.
The guardian erased the consensual debts. You tried to stop the erasing. Return when restoring consent is more powerful than stopping erasure.
codex: The Debt-Market tests whether the deity can resist the Hollow's gifts. The defense is ignoring — not accepting or refusing. In the Infernal Gate, ignored debts become unowned. Let them float.

The free debts are lighter because they have been given 'freely' — but the Hollow's freedom means without consent from either party. A debt without consent is not a debt. It is theft disguised as a gift.
The debt-givers offer useful obligations. The usefulness is the bait. The defense is ignoring — because both acceptance and refusal acknowledge the system. Ignoring denies the system's existence.

The original ledger records consensual transactions. The Hollow erases them to free the debts. Freeing a consensual debt without consent is not freedom. It is theft. The restoration is restoring consent.

intro: The Chain of Unpaid Debts. The Infernal Gate's enforcement mechanism has been corrupted. The Hollow has broken the chain's links, creating a cascade of unpaid debts that each generate their own chains.
The cascading chains are multiplying. Each unpaid debt creates a new chain binding new debtors to new creditors — all without consent. The chain is self-replicating.
The self-replicating chains have reached the trial road. Each step creates new debt — the road itself is a creditor, charging for passage. The deity must walk a road that costs with every step.
The chain's origin. The first link — the original binding: 'I consent to be bound.' The Hollow corrupted it: 'I am bound without consent.'
enemy: Chain-constructs born from unpaid debts. Each one is a self-replicating binding that creates new debt with every contact. Touching one means owing one.
The chains are cascading exponentially. Each new debt creates a new chain.
Hollow chain-forgers creating new links by breaking old ones. Each broken link releases two new ones.
The first link's guardian — a Hollow wearing the first chain. It speaks the corrupted binding: 'I am bound without consent.'
mid: The chain-constructs create debt on contact. Do not touch them. In the Infernal Gate, contact is consent. Avoid contact to avoid consent.
The cascading chains are exponential. Do not fight the cascade — cut the source. The source is the corrupted first link.
The chain-forgers break links to create more. Do not stop the breaking. Forge a new first link — a consensual link that does not need to replicate.
The guardian speaks the corrupted binding. Speak the original: 'I consent to be bound.' The consent is the binding. Without consent, the chain is slavery. Restore consent.
victory: The first chain is stabilized. The cascade is slowed — but the self-replicating chains remain. The deeper chambers will have faster cascades.
The chain-constructs are controlled — but the debt they generated remains. The Infernal Gate does not forgive debt. It transfers it.
The chain-forgers are silenced — but their forged links remain. Each forged link is a binding without consent.
The first link is restored. The original binding is re-established. But the corrupted links remain. The restoration is a new link, not a replacement.
defeat: The chain-constructs created debt on contact. You touched them. Return when avoidance is more powerful than contact.
The cascading chains were exponential. You fought the cascade instead of the source. Return when cutting the source is more powerful.
The chain-forgers created more by breaking. You tried to stop the breaking. Return when forging a new first link is more powerful.
The guardian's corrupted binding held. You argued. Return when speaking the original is more powerful than arguing with the corrupted version.
codex: The Chain of Unpaid Debts tests whether the deity can navigate a system where enforcement has become self-replicating. A binding without consent replicates because it has no legitimate holder.
The self-replicating chains create debt on contact. The Hollow has made contact mandatory. The defense is cutting the source — the corrupted first link.
The chain-forgers break links to create more. The defense is forging a new first link that does not need to replicate because it is consensually complete.
The first link was 'I consent to be bound.' The Hollow corrupted it to 'I am bound without consent.' A chain with consent is a debt. A chain without consent is slavery.

intro: The Debtors' Revolt. The debtors of the Infernal Gate have been incited to revolt by the Hollow. The promise: break your chains and be free. The lie: breaking chains in the Infernal Gate creates new debt.
The revolt is spreading. Each debtor who breaks their chain generates a new debt — the debt of breaking. The new debt is larger than the original. The revolt makes everyone more indebted.
The revolt has reached the trial road. Debtors break chains everywhere. Each broken chain releases a shockwave of new debt. The road is drowning in debt-shockwaves.
The revolt's origin. The first debtor has been freed by the Hollow — but the freeing created a new debt: the debt of being freed without consent. The first debtor is more bound now than before.
enemy: Revolting debtors breaking their chains. They are not enemies — they are victims of the Hollow's promise. Each believes they are being freed. Each is being more bound.
The debtors break chains faster. Each broken chain creates a shockwave of new debt, destabilizing the Gate's ledger system.
Hollow revolutionaries inciting debtors to break chains. Each broken chain feeds the Hollow. The revolution is the feeding strategy.
The first debtor's liberator — a Hollow wearing the original creditor's face. It freed the debtor without consent. The debt of unwanted liberation is the largest debt in the Gate.
mid: The revolting debtors are victims. Do not fight them — restore their chains. The chains were consensual. The breaking is not. Restore consent.
The broken chains create shockwaves. Do not fight the shockwaves — absorb them. Carry the debt temporarily, then transfer it when consent is restored.
The revolutionaries incite breaking. Do not silence them — out-argue them. The Hollow says breaking is freedom. The truth: breaking creates new debt.
The liberator freed the debtor without consent. Do not re-bind — restore the consent. Ask. If the debtor consents to the original debt, the chain is restored. If not, the debt is void.
victory: The first revolt is calmed. Some debtors restored their chains consensually. Some voided their debts. Both are legitimate. The deeper chambers will have more revolts.
The broken chains are restored — but the new debt remains. The deity carries the revolt's debt. The deeper chambers will be heavier.
The revolutionaries are out-argued — but their promise echoes. 'Break your chains and be free.' The deeper chambers will have louder revolutionaries.
The first debtor is restored. The consent was asked — and the debtor chose the original debt. But the debt of unwanted liberation remains.
defeat: The revolting debtors were victims. You fought them. Return when restoring is more powerful than fighting.
The broken chains created shockwaves. You fought them instead of absorbing. Return when carrying and transferring is more powerful.
The revolutionaries' promise was seductive. You silenced them. Return when truth is more powerful than suppression.
The liberator freed without consent. You re-bound without asking. Return when asking is more powerful than binding.
codex: The Debtors' Revolt tests whether the deity can restore a system where enforcement has been weaponized through false liberation. Breaking chains creates more debt. The freedom is the trap.
The revolting debtors are victims. The Hollow incites them with a promise. The defense is restoring consent. A consensual chain is a debt. A broken consensual chain is a bigger debt.

The revolutionaries incite breaking because each broken chain feeds the Hollow. The defense is out-arguing — the truth is verifiable. Break a chain and the debt grows. The Hollow can only promise otherwise.
The debt of being freed without consent is the Infernal Gate's deepest lesson: freedom without consent is not freedom. It is a different kind of binding. Consent is the only resolution.

intro: The Throne of Unowned Debt. The final trial. Every erased debt, every free obligation, every broken chain, every unconsented liberation — assembled into a throne of unowned debt. The Hollow sits on it, unbound.
The Unowned Debt Throne radiates unowned obligations. Every debt on it has no creditor and no debtor. The throne is the largest unowned obligation — binding the entire Gate to the Hollow.

The throne has consumed the first transaction, the original ledger, the first chain, and the first debtor's consent. All say: all debt is unowned. All binding is without consent. The Infernal Gate is a system of slavery.
The final confrontation. The throne's claim: all debt is slavery. All consent is coerced. Disprove it — with a consensual transaction the throne cannot un-own.
enemy: The Throne of Unowned Debt radiating unowned obligations. The throne itself is the largest unowned obligation — binding the entire Gate to the Hollow.
The throne spawns unowned constructs — debts with no owner that attach to the deity, adding unconsensual weight.
Hollow un-owners erasing ownership from every debt the deity holds. Each erased ownership turns consensual debt into unowned obligation.
The throne speaking with four voices: the first transaction, the first ledger, the first chain, the first debtor. All say: all debt is slavery.
mid: The throne radiates unowned obligations. Do not resist them — own them. The Hollow un-owns to make them float. The defense is owning — consensually. An owned debt is not slavery.
The unowned constructs attach without consent. Do not remove them — consent to them. Consent transforms unowned obligation into consensual debt. The debt remains. The slavery does not.
The un-owners erase ownership. Do not protect old ownership — create new. Each re-owning is a new act of consent. The Hollow un-owns. The deity re-owns.
The throne claims all debt is slavery. Disprove it — with a consensual transaction. The throne cannot un-own a transaction where both parties consent. Consent is a choice. Choices cannot be erased.
victory: The Throne of Unowned Debt is shattered. The unowned debts are re-owned — through new acts of consent. The first transaction, the original ledger, the first chain, the first debtor — all restored. All consensual. The Black-Iron Gate is damaged but not destroyed.
The unowned constructs are dissolved — through consent. The deity owned each one consensually. The ownership transformed slavery into transaction. The debt remains. The slavery does not.
The un-owners are starved. They erased ownership — and the deity re-owned. Consent cannot be erased because it is not a thing. It is a choice. The choice was made.

The throne's claim is disproved: not all debt is slavery. Debt without consent is slavery. Debt with consent is a transaction. The difference is consent. The Black-Iron Gate stands — sustained by consent, by choice, by agreement.
defeat: The throne radiated unowned obligations. You resisted instead of owning. Return when consent is more powerful than resistance.
The unowned constructs attached without consent. You removed them. Return when consent transforms slavery into transaction.
The un-owners erased your ownership. You protected it. Return when re-owning is more powerful than protecting.
The throne's claim held. You could not disprove it. Return when a consensual transaction is undeniable — when consent proves debt is not slavery.
codex: The Throne of Unowned Debt is the Hollow's ultimate Infernal weapon: every unowned obligation assembled into one throne. The disproof is not argument — it is act. A consensual transaction the throne cannot un-own.
The unowned constructs attach without consent. The defense is consent. Consent transforms unowned obligation into consensual debt. The debt is not the slavery. The absence of consent is the slavery.
The un-owners erase ownership. The defense is re-owning — creating new ownership through new acts of consent. Consent cannot be erased because it is not a thing. It is an act.

The Infernal Gate's deepest truth: debt without consent is slavery. Debt with consent is a transaction. The difference is consent. The Hollow erases consent to turn transactions into slavery. The deity restores consent to turn slavery back into transactions.

intro: The ledger has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign debt-data. Every transaction you restored, every consent you established, every chain you reforged is recorded — and the Hollow has learned from each.
The corrupted debts now carry your Normal campaign consent as evidence. They argue your consent was coerced by the Gate.
The chain system expects your Normal campaign approach. Every technique has been analyzed and countered.
The final trial has been re-ledgered. The Normal campaign victory is recorded — and the Elite version asks whether your consent was real or whether the Gate demanded it.
enemy: Elite unowned obligations carrying your Normal campaign consent-data. They target the debts you took.
The corrupted debts argue your consent was coerced. Each uses your Normal campaign choices as evidence.
The chain system counters your Normal campaign approach. The Hollow has new un-owning methods.
The re-ledgered trial guardian speaks with your Normal campaign voice. It asks: did you consent, or did the Gate make you consent?
mid: The obligations target the debts you took. Take different ones. Create new consent.
The coercion argument holds. Do not argue back — consent again. New consent disproves old coercion.
The chain system counters your approach. Create new consent the Hollow has not seen.
The guardian questions your consent. Answer with a new consensual transaction — one that proves consent was choice.
victory: Chapter 1 holds — but the ledger has recorded this consent too. The deeper chambers will question it.
The corrupted debts are silenced — but their coercion argument echoes. The deeper chambers will argue louder.
The chain system is restored — but with new techniques. The Hollow will analyze these too.
The guardian falls — but the question remains. The Elite answer: the consent was real because it was new. Coerced consent repeats. Free consent creates.
defeat: The obligations targeted the debts you took. You took the same ones. Return when new consent is more powerful than old patterns.
The coercion argument held. You argued. Return when new consent is the only answer to old coercion.
The chain system countered your approach. You restored the same way. Return when creating new consent is more powerful than repeating.
The guardian's question held. Return when new consensual transactions are undeniable proof of free choice.
codex: The Elite Chapter 1 stores debt-data across campaigns. Every Normal consent becomes an Elite vulnerability.
The Gate's learning engine spans multiple campaigns. Each descent teaches the Hollow which debts the deity consents to.
The Elite chain system studies Normal campaign restoration. The deity must create new consent — because repetition is not consent. It is compliance.
Each Elite victory teaches the Gate how to un-own the next deity's consent. The ledger is an archive of every consent ever given.

intro: The Throne of Unowned Debt has been rebuilt with your Normal campaign consent. It carries your consent as its foundation — your Normal campaign consensual transactions, consumed and un-owned. The throne claims YOUR consent proves all consent is coerced.

The throne uses your Normal campaign consent to un-own ALL consent. Each consensual transaction is presented as evidence that consent under the Gate is always coerced. Your choices, weaponized against choice itself.
The throne speaks with five voices — the first transaction, the first ledger, the first chain, the first debtor, AND your Normal campaign voice. All say: all consent is coerced.
The final Elite confrontation. The throne's claim: across both campaigns, your consent proves the Gate coerces. Disprove it — with consent that no Gate could coerce.
enemy: Elite Throne of Unowned Debt with your Normal campaign consent. Your consensual transactions, weaponized as evidence of coercion.
The throne spawns constructs from your Normal campaign consent. Each is a consensual transaction you performed — now un-owned and presented as coerced.
Hollow consent-corrupters re-labeling consent as compliance. Each act of consent becomes compliance. The re-labeling is the weapon.
The final throne — speaking with five voices. The claim: your consent proves all consent is coerced. Disprove it.
mid: The throne uses your consent against you. Do not deny your old consent — re-consent. New consent is the answer. Create consent it has not seen.
The constructs are your transactions re-labeled as coerced. Do not defend old consent — perform new consent. The defense of consent is not argument. It is act.
The consent-corrupters re-label consent as compliance. Do not resist — demonstrate the difference. Compliance repeats. Consent creates. Create something new.
The throne claims all consent is coerced. Disprove it — with consent that creates. Coercion cannot create. Only consent can. The creation is the proof.
victory: The throne is shattered for the last time. Your Normal campaign consent is freed. The consent was not coerced. The proof: you consented again, differently, creating something new. Coercion repeats. Consent creates. The Black-Iron Gate is damaged but not destroyed.
The constructs are dissolved. Your transactions are restored — not as evidence of coercion, but as proof of choice. Coerced consent repeats identically. Free consent creates anew.
The consent-corrupters are starved. They re-labeled consent as compliance — but the deity created. Compliance cannot create. Only consent can. The creation is the proof.

The Throne of Unowned Debt is destroyed for the last time. The claim is disproved: consent that creates is free. Consent that repeats is compliance. The Infernal Gate stands — sustained by consent that creates, by choice that produces, by freedom that generates. The consent was free because the creation was new.
defeat: The throne used your consent against you. You denied your old consent. Return when re-consenting is more powerful than denying.
The constructs were your transactions re-labeled. You defended your old consent. Return when new consent is more powerful than defending.
The consent-corrupters re-labeled everything. You resisted. Return when creating is more powerful than resisting.
The throne's claim held. Return when consent that creates — consent that produces something new — is the undeniable proof of freedom.
codex: The Elite Throne of Unowned Debt is the Infernal Gate's ultimate trial: the deity's own consent, consumed and weaponized. The disproof requires consent that no pressure could produce.
The consent-corrupters re-label consent as compliance. Compliance repeats. Consent creates. The defense is not arguing that consent was free — it is demonstrating freedom through creation.

The Elite final claim resolves the Infernal Gate's deepest question: is consent under the Gate's pressure truly free? The answer: consent that creates is free. Consent that repeats is compliance. The difference is creation.

The Elite Final Verdict: consent is not coerced because it occurs under pressure. Consent is coerced when it repeats what the pressure demands. Consent is free when it creates what the pressure could not demand. Coercion repeats. Consent creates. The creation is the proof. The consent was free because the creation was new.
